stem: You never saved last week's job IDs. Which approaches let you locate and retrieve those jobs? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Call `service.jobs(...)` with filters such as `backend_name` or `created_after` to list matching jobs
Iterate the returned jobs and call `.result()` on the one you want
Look up the job and its ID on the Workloads page of IBM Quantum Platform
Call `service.job()` without a job ID -- it then returns your whole job history
Load them with `json.load(file, cls=RuntimeDecoder)` from the JSON file Runtime saves locally for each job
Resubmit the same circuit with `sampler.run(...)`; Runtime returns the cached original result

explanation.correct: `service.jobs()` returns your recent jobs and accepts filters (`backend_name`, `created_after`, `session_id`, `pending`, ...); you then call `.result()` on the job you want. The IBM Quantum Platform Workloads page lists your submitted jobs together with their IDs (the save-jobs guide points there for exactly this purpose). Results are stored server-side, so a kernel restart does not lose them.

distractors.D: `service.job()` is the singular lookup and requires a job ID (`TypeError` without one); listing many jobs is what the plural `service.jobs()` does, and it pages with `limit` (default 10) rather than dumping everything.
distractors.E: Saving to disk is opt-in: the save-jobs guide has YOU call `json.dump(result, file, cls=RuntimeEncoder)`, and qiskit-ibm-runtime itself writes no result files (in 0.48 its only file writes are saved account credentials). With no file of your own, the server-side copy reached through `service.jobs(...)` is the way back.
distractors.F: Runtime does not deduplicate submissions: an identical PUB is a NEW job with a new ID, new queue time and freshly sampled shots. Retrieval is by job ID, not by circuit content.

provenance.notes: adversarial s7: D/E rephrased without absolute wording (kills absolute-distractor tell); Workloads-page option C confirmed against the live save-jobs guide | pool wave: +F Runtime returns a cached result for an identical resubmission | realism audit 2026-10-01: stem trimmed; 2->1, documented service.jobs filters + Workloads page | adversarial A3 2026-10-16: E was a non-approach statement (easy elimination in a 'which approaches' list) -> rewritten as the auto-saved-local-JSON misconception; 0.48 source grep: only accounts/storage.py writes files; signature check jobs(limit=10, backend_name, created_after, session_id, pending, ...); citations verified (save-jobs: 'see all your submitted jobs and their IDs on the Workloads page')
